objective: Research and calculate the auto-compact window that minimizes cost for HolyAgent's Opus 5.5 root without hurting quality, and say whether a default better than 450000 tokens exists.
scope: Cost model: each root call re-reads its whole context as cache reads (Opus 5.5: $4/MTok input, cache write 1.25x for 5m and 2x for 1h TTL, cache read 0.1x? check the pricing page: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing) plus new tokens; context grows by g tokens per call from a post-compaction base B; compaction at window W costs a summarization call (reads W, writes a summary) and a cold cache rewrite of the new prefix. Derive cost per call averaged over a compaction cycle as a function of W, B, g, and find the minimizing W analytically (it should be around sqrt-type optimum: W* = B + sqrt(2*g*C_compact/r_read)-style); compute numbers for plausible B (30k-80k: system prompt + tools + rules + summary) and g (2k-15k per call), and include compaction quality loss as a qualitative constraint.

Quality evidence: long-context degradation (context rot) studies and Anthropic/OpenAI guidance on compaction; Claude Code's default (~967K for 1M models) and its /autocompact range 100K-1M; Codex: compaction at 90% of window, GPT 6.1 Sol 500k window (derived ~450k).
The repo's own numbers: docs/decisions.md (root grew to 365-747k tokens per call; predecessor compacted 4 times discarding ~2.9M cache tokens).
constraints: Show the formula, the assumptions and a small table of W vs cost per call for 3-4 (B, g) scenarios; mark assumptions vs sourced prices. Conclude with a recommended default and whether it beats 450000 meaningfully; if the optimum is flat around 450k say so.

You may run arithmetic with a quick script in your scratch area outside the repository; read-only for the repo. Keep working until done; stop and report. Report in under 600 words; put the full table in a file outside the repository and give its path.

calculation: table of W vs cost for several scenarios and the optimum
verdict: whether a better default than 450000 exists, with quality caveats

result:
result: Cost-only optimum is 115k–385k, below 450k, and moves with g. 450k is within 1% to 42% of optimal total cost per call across four scenarios (about 7% to 16% in the two mid cases). I recommend 300k as the default, a modest gain of about 3% to 15% over 450k in three of four scenarios; 450k stays defensible if compaction quality is the priority.

**Sourced prices** (Anthropic pricing page, fetched 2026-11-03, Opus 5.5; page covers current models):
- Input is $4/MTok, 5m cache write $5, 1h cache write $8, output $20.
- Cache read is $0.20/MTok. That is 0.05x input, not the 0.1x in the brief; the page footnote says Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 use 0.05x.

**Model.** Let r = 0.2, w = 5 ($/MTok, 5m TTL), o = 20, S = summary tokens, B = base after compaction, g = growth per call, x = W − B, n = x/g calls per cycle.
- Per-call cost = r(B+W)/2 + C_c/n + [w·g + o·out]. The bracket does not depend on W.
- Compaction cost C_c = r·W (summarizer read) + o·S + w·B (cold rewrite of the new prefix).
- Setting the derivative to zero gives **W\* = B + sqrt(2·g·((r+w)·B + o·S)/r)**. With a 1h TTL (w = 8) the optimum rises, for example from 265k to about 297k at B=50, g=10.
- Assumptions, not sourced:
  - S = 10k tokens.
  - Output is 1.5k tokens per call.
  - Every call hits the cache within the TTL.
  - The summarizer call reads W from cache.
  - There is no long-context surcharge for Opus 5.5 (none shown on the page).
  - Subagent context is ignored.

**Table.** Cost per call in $ is the W-dependent part, with total (including the constant part) in parentheses. The constant part is 0.04 (B=30, g=2), 0.055 (B=50, g=5), 0.08 (B=50, g=10) and 0.105 (B=80, g=15).

| W (k tokens) | B=30, g=2 | B=50, g=5 | B=50, g=10 | B=80, g=15 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 114 (optimum, first column) | 0.0233 (0.063) | | | |
| 150 | | 0.044 | 0.068 | |
| 200 | 0.0276 | 0.0413 (0.096, optimum at 202) | 0.0577 | 0.108 |
| 265 (optimum, third column) | | | 0.0549 (0.135) | |
| 300 | 0.036 (0.076) | 0.0452 (0.100) | 0.0554 (0.135) | 0.0829 (0.188) |
| 384 (optimum, fourth column) | | | | 0.0797 (0.185) |
| 450 | 0.050 (0.090) | 0.0568 (0.112) | 0.0635 (0.144) | 0.0809 (0.186) |
| 700 | | | 0.0841 | 0.0959 |
| 967 (Claude Code default) | 0.1009 (0.141) | 0.1052 (0.160) | 0.1087 (0.189) | 0.1181 (0.223) |

Totals at 450k versus the optimum in each scenario:

| Scenario | 450k vs optimum |
|---|---|
| B=30, g=2 | +42% |
| B=50, g=5 | +16% |
| B=50, g=10 | +7% |
| B=80, g=15 | +1% (flat) |

The 967k default costs 20% to 120% more than the optimum. The curve rises slowly above the optimum and steeply below it. At B=80, g=15, W=200 costs about 30% more than the 384k optimum.

300k is the minimax choice. It is within 0.4% to 4% of the optimum in three scenarios and +20% in the light-growth case, versus 450k's +1% to +42%. The repo records root growth to 365–747k tokens per call and the predecessor's four compactions discarding about 2.9M cache tokens (docs/decisions.md lines 19–20). Together these suggest high g, where 300–450k is nearly flat.

**Quality evidence.**
- Chroma "Context Rot" (July 2025, 18 models including Claude 4) found performance degrades as input grows. It tested older models, so the size of the effect on Opus 5.5 is unknown.
- Anthropic's context-engineering post (2025-09-29) says compaction is lossy and "overly aggressive compaction" drops subtle context.
- Each additional compaction adds loss. Lower W means more frequent compaction, so the cost savings trade against quality that I could not quantify.
- Claude Code docs: `/autocompact` accepts 100K–1M, the default for native-1M models is about 967K, and the per-model `modelSettings` entry beats the top-level key.
- A secondary source (SpecWeave) says the Claude Code team recommends 400k. I did not verify this.
- Codex (OpenAI issue #10365): auto-compaction at 90% of the window, and since v0.100.0 the limit is clamped to 90% (issue #11805).
- Conflict with the brief: a secondary source (finopsllm, Codex 0.157.1) says GPT-6 Sol gets a 272k window and compacts at 244.8k, not a 500k window and 450k. I could not confirm which is right.

**claude.ai/Claude Code configuration to document.**
- Set `modelSettings["claude-opus-5-5"].autoCompactWindow`, or use `/autocompact`, `--autocompact`, or the `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW` environment variable.
- The environment variable overrides everything else, and managed settings preempt `/autocompact` but not the flag.
- The window is capped at the model's context window and accepts 100K–1M.
- `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT=1` forces compaction at 200K.
- A gateway that rejects requests above 200K needs `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW=200000`.

**Atomic commits request.** I did not research the squash-merge and atomic-commits item; it needs no research, only a docs and rubric rule for the root.
